sections.content: You know the sequence of tenses (*ayudara*) from B1 Unit 38: a past main verb takes the imperfect subjunctive after *que* (*pidió que se revisara*), and a present main verb takes the present subjunctive (*pide que se revise*). Formal reports often put both in one paragraph: they tell what happened with *pidió* and say what still stands with *ha pedido*. The present perfect looks back from now, so it normally goes with the present: the request is still current and the verb after *que* is present. The verb after *que* follows the main verb, not the date of the report.

sections.title: Main verb and verb after que
rows: La comisión pide que se revise el texto.
The committee asks for the text to be revised. (present: present subjunctive)
La comisión ha pedido que se revise el texto.
The committee has asked for the text to be revised. (perfect: present subjunctive)
La comisión pidió que se revisara el texto.
The committee asked for the text to be revised. (indefinido: imperfect subjunctive)
La comisión pedía que se revisara el texto.
The committee used to ask for the text to be revised. (imperfect: imperfect subjunctive)

items.spanish: La comisión ha recomendado que se publique el dictamen.
items.english: The committee has recommended that the formal opinion be published.

items.spanish: El director exigió que se entregara el borrador antes del plazo.
items.english: The director demanded that the draft be handed in before the deadline.

items.spanish: El acta indica que la comisión pidió que se corrigieran las erratas.
items.english: The minutes say that the committee asked for the misprints to be corrected.

items.spanish: En la sesión de hoy se ha propuesto que se apruebe la enmienda.
items.english: At today’s session it has been proposed that the amendment be approved.

sections.content: In a report the usual slip is mixing the two. In a finished past frame (*el martes pasado*, *ayer*) use the imperfect subjunctive. The present subjunctive after a past verb is possible only when the action still lies ahead at the moment of speaking. Check the main verb first. *Pidió*, *exigió* and *recomendó* take the imperfect subjunctive (*-ara*, *-iera*); *pide*, *ha pedido* and *recomienda* take the present subjunctive (*-e*, *-a*). The same holds when *se* hides who asks: *se pidió que se revisara*, *se ha pedido que se revise*.
